newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil IBGE sees coffee cherry crop down 7.90 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil IBGE sees coffee cherry crop down 7.90 pct.

text.p: Brazil's coffee crop in 1997 should reach 2.23 million tonnes in cherry, down 7.90 percent from last year, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said in a statement.
IBGE issues its figure in cherry, whereas other forecasts are normally in green coffee beans. Agronomists say there is no reliable formula to convert cherry estimates to beans.
The IBGE said it still has to receive information from Sao Paulo and Parana states.
But Minas Gerais and Espirito Santo are expected to see respective falls of 10.29 percent and 10.08 percent in output.

Area given over to coffee trees in both states is practically the same as last year but there are anticipated falls in productivity, the IBGE said. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
